Kitchen Remodeling in St. Louis

Transform your kitchen into a space designed around the way you live.

Aptitude Design & Build provides custom kitchen remodeling in St. Louis, St. Charles, and surrounding communities. From improving an outdated layout to creating an open-concept kitchen with custom cabinetry, better storage, and more room to gather, we design and build kitchens that work beautifully for everyday life.

As a full-service design-build remodeling company, we manage your kitchen remodel from initial planning and design through construction and completion. That means one team working together on your layout, selections, budget, construction, and all the details in between.

Whether you’re remodeling an older St. Louis home or rethinking a kitchen that simply no longer works for your family, we can help you determine what’s possible and create a plan to bring it to life.

Custom Kitchen Remodeling Designed Around Your Home

A successful kitchen remodel starts with understanding what isn’t working.

Maybe you need more storage. Your island is too small. The kitchen feels cut off from the rest of the house. There isn’t enough room for everyone to gather. Or perhaps the kitchen simply feels dated and no longer reflects the rest of your home.

We look at the kitchen as part of the entire house — considering how you cook, entertain, move through the space, and connect the kitchen to adjacent dining and living areas.

Depending on your home and goals, your kitchen remodel may include:

Custom cabinetry and storage solutions
Kitchen islands
Layout redesign
Wall removal and open-concept design
Countertops and backsplashes
Lighting and electrical upgrades
Flooring
Appliance integration
Walk-in or built-in pantries
Custom range hoods and ventilation
Beverage stations and coffee bars
Plumbing and fixture updates
Architectural and finish details

The goal isn’t simply to make your kitchen look different. It’s to create a kitchen that functions better and feels like it belongs in your home.

Kitchen Remodeling vs. Kitchen Renovation: What Do You Need?

Kitchen remodeling and kitchen renovation are often used interchangeably, but there can be an important difference.

A kitchen renovation generally updates an existing kitchen without substantially changing its layout or function. This might include replacing cabinetry, countertops, flooring, lighting, or appliances while keeping the basic footprint intact.

A kitchen remodel can go further, changing how the kitchen is configured and used. That may involve removing walls, changing the floor plan, relocating appliances or plumbing, creating a larger island, adding storage, or connecting the kitchen more naturally to surrounding spaces.

Not every kitchen needs a completely new layout. If your existing configuration works well, keeping it may allow you to invest more of your budget in cabinetry, appliances, countertops, and finishes.

But if the layout is the problem, a remodel gives you the opportunity to solve it.

READ: Kitchen Remodeling vs. Kitchen Renovation: What’s the Difference — and Which Do You Need?

Kitchen Remodeling for Older St. Louis Homes

Older homes are one of the things that make St. Louis neighborhoods so distinctive — but remodeling their kitchens can require a different approach.

Many older kitchens were designed for a very different way of living. They may be smaller and more enclosed, with limited storage, fewer electrical outlets, outdated plumbing, or little connection to nearby living and dining spaces.

Depending on the age and condition of the house, remodeling may also uncover uneven floors, older wiring, previous renovations, plumbing issues, plaster walls, or structural conditions that need to be addressed.

That doesn’t mean stripping away everything that gives an older home character.

Thoughtful remodeling can create a kitchen that functions for modern life while still feeling appropriate for the architecture of the house. Cabinetry, millwork, flooring, lighting, materials, proportions, and architectural details can all help connect the new kitchen to the rest of the home.

Our team considers both what you want the kitchen to become and what the existing house is telling us.

Can You Change Your Kitchen Layout?

Yes. And for some homeowners, changing the layout is what makes the biggest difference.

A kitchen remodel can potentially include removing a wall, relocating appliances, moving plumbing, changing doorways, creating a larger island, expanding storage, or improving the connection between the kitchen and adjacent rooms.

But changing the layout simply for the sake of changing it can add unnecessary cost.

We start by asking whether the existing layout supports the way you want to live.

If it does, we may be able to create a dramatic transformation without moving everything. If it doesn’t, we can explore what changes would meaningfully improve the space and what those changes involve from a construction and budget standpoint.

How Much Does a Kitchen Remodel Cost in St. Louis?

Kitchen remodeling costs vary significantly depending on the size of the kitchen, project scope, cabinetry, appliances, materials, layout changes, and complexity of construction.

A kitchen renovation that keeps the existing footprint and focuses primarily on finishes will require a different investment than a remodel involving custom cabinetry, relocated plumbing, structural changes, premium appliances, or a completely redesigned layout.

Some of the biggest factors affecting kitchen remodeling costs include:

Cabinetry
Layout changes
Structural work
Countertops
Appliances
Plumbing
Electrical work
Flooring
Lighting
Fixtures and finishes
Existing conditions within the home

Rather than selecting a generic remodeling budget based on square footage alone, we recommend considering what you want to accomplish and what level of investment makes sense for your home.

READ: How Much Should You Spend on a Kitchen Remodel Based on Your Home’s Value?

Why Choose Design-Build for a Kitchen Remodel?

Kitchen remodeling requires a lot of decisions — and many of those decisions affect one another.

Moving a range can affect ventilation and electrical requirements. Changing the size of an island can affect circulation and lighting. Cabinetry decisions influence appliance placement, countertops, storage, and budget.

With a traditional approach, design and construction may be handled by different companies.

A design-build approach brings those pieces together.

At Aptitude Design & Build, the people responsible for building your kitchen are involved in the planning process. Design, construction, material selections, feasibility, and budget can be considered together rather than treated as separate stages.

For homeowners, that creates a more coordinated process and helps identify potential construction or budget considerations before work begins.

Our Kitchen Remodeling Process
1. Consultation

We start by learning about your home, your kitchen, what isn’t working, what you’d like to change, and your priorities for the project.

This is also an opportunity to talk about your anticipated investment and determine whether your goals and budget are aligned.

2. Design and Layout Planning

Next, we develop a plan for the kitchen.

Depending on the project, this may involve exploring different layouts, cabinetry configurations, islands, storage solutions, appliance placement, lighting, and connections to adjacent rooms.

This is where we answer the bigger question: How can this kitchen work better?

3. Selections and Budgeting

Once the direction is established, we help you work through cabinetry, countertops, flooring, fixtures, lighting, appliances, hardware, and other materials.

Because design and construction are integrated, selections can be considered alongside the overall project budget.

4. Pre-Construction Planning

Before construction begins, we coordinate the details required to build the project, including plans, scheduling, trade coordination, ordering, and permitting when required.

Good preparation at this stage helps create a smoother construction process.

5. Construction and Project Management

Our team manages the construction process from demolition through completion.

Depending on the project, that may include structural work, framing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, flooring, cabinetry, countertops, tile, lighting, painting, and finish carpentry.

6. Final Walkthrough

At the end of the project, we complete a final walkthrough and address the remaining details before your kitchen is complete.

How Long Does a Kitchen Remodel Take?

Most kitchen remodels take approximately 8–12 weeks once construction begins, although the timeline depends on the scope and complexity of the project.

A kitchen that remains within its existing footprint may take less time than a major remodel involving structural work, wall removal, custom cabinetry, relocated plumbing, or significant layout changes.

It’s also important to distinguish between construction time and the total remodeling process. Design, material selections, cabinetry ordering, permitting, and pre-construction planning happen before demolition begins.

Starting those conversations early gives your team more time to plan the project properly.

Why Choose Aptitude Design & Build for Your Kitchen Remodel?

We believe a great kitchen should do more than photograph well.

It should work.

Aptitude brings design and construction together to create kitchens that respond to the home and the people living in it. Our team can help you think through everything from major layout changes and structural considerations to cabinetry, lighting, storage, materials, and the small details that make the finished kitchen feel cohesive.

Full-service design-build remodeling

From the first conversation to the final walkthrough, our goal is to make both the kitchen and the remodeling process work better.

Kitchen Remodeling FAQs
How much does a kitchen remodel cost in St. Louis?

The cost of a kitchen remodel depends on the size and scope of the project, cabinetry, appliances, materials, and whether the project involves structural or layout changes. A kitchen that keeps its existing footprint will generally require a different investment than a custom remodel involving wall removal, relocated plumbing, custom cabinetry, or premium appliances.

For a more detailed breakdown, see our Kitchen Remodel Cost in St. Louis guide.

How long does a kitchen remodel take?

Most kitchen remodels take approximately 8–12 weeks once construction begins. Larger or more complex projects involving structural changes, custom cabinetry, or substantial layout changes may take longer. Design, selections, ordering, and pre-construction planning take place before construction begins.

Do you design the kitchen as well as build it?

Yes. Aptitude is a full-service design-build remodeling company. We work with homeowners on the design and planning of the kitchen and manage construction through completion.

Can you remove a wall to create an open-concept kitchen?

In many homes, yes. Whether a wall can be removed — and what is required to remove it — depends on the structure of the house. Our team evaluates the existing conditions and develops a plan for structural changes when appropriate.

Can I change the location of my sink or appliances?

Often, yes. Sinks, ranges, refrigerators, dishwashers, and other appliances can potentially be relocated as part of a kitchen remodel. Moving them may require plumbing, electrical, gas, ventilation, or other construction work, so we consider those requirements as part of the overall design.

Do you provide custom cabinetry?

Yes. Custom cabinetry and storage design can be incorporated into Aptitude kitchen remodeling projects. Cabinetry can be designed around your kitchen layout, storage needs, appliances, and overall design.

Can I live in my house during a kitchen remodel?

Many homeowners remain in their homes during a kitchen remodel, although you should expect your kitchen to be unavailable for portions of construction. We can help you understand the expected construction schedule so you can plan for temporary cooking and other day-to-day adjustments.

Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in St. Louis?

It depends on the scope of work and the jurisdiction. Projects involving structural, plumbing, electrical, or other substantial changes may require permits and inspections. Aptitude coordinates required permitting for the remodeling projects we manage.

How far in advance should I start planning my kitchen remodel?

Earlier is generally better, particularly for a substantial remodel. Design development, material selections, cabinetry lead times, permitting, and pre-construction planning all happen before construction begins.

Starting early gives you more time to make thoughtful decisions rather than rushing through design and selections to meet a construction date.

Do I need to know exactly what I want before contacting you?

No.

In fact, many homeowners contact us because they know their current kitchen isn't working but aren't sure what the best solution is.

That's part of the design-build process. We can help you evaluate the existing space, identify priorities, explore possibilities, and determine what makes sense for your home and budget.

Basement Remodeling & Finishing in St. Louis

Aptitude Design & Build is a full-service basement remodeling and finishing contractor serving homeowners throughout St. Louis, St. Charles and surrounding Missouri communities. From unfinished basements to outdated lower levels, our design-build team transforms underused spaces into comfortable, functional living areas designed around the way your family lives.

Whether you’re creating a home office, entertainment space, guest suite, workout room, custom bar or additional family living area, we manage your basement renovation from design and space planning through construction and finishing. The result is a thoughtfully designed space that maximizes your home's square footage, comfort and long-term value.

- Basement finishing
- Custom basement layouts and space planning
- Home bars and entertainment areas
- Home theaters and media rooms

How Much Does a Basement Remodel Cost in St. Louis?

Basement remodeling costs in St. Louis vary based on the size of the basement, level of finish, plumbing and electrical requirements, and features included in the design. Bathrooms, custom bars, guest suites, home theaters and structural modifications can all increase the overall investment.

For detailed St. Louis pricing, see our Basement Remodel Cost Guide →

Benefits of Finishing a Basement

Finishing a basement can significantly expand your usable living space without the cost of building an addition. Many homeowners in St. Louis choose basement remodeling projects to create more room for entertaining, working from home, accommodating growing families, or increasing resale value.

A finished basement can provide:

- Additional living and entertaining space
- Increased home value
- More flexible square footage
- Dedicated guest accommodations
- Private work or fitness areas
- Improved storage and organization
Our Design-Build Basement Remodeling Process
Design Consultation

We begin by understanding how you want to use the space and identifying opportunities to improve layout, comfort, and functionality.

Concept and Space Planning

Material Selections and Budgeting

Construction and Project Management

Final Walkthrough and Completion

Many homeowners throughout St. Louis and St. Charles are transforming basements into:

- Family entertainment spaces
- Sports viewing rooms
- Home gyms
- Golf simulator rooms
- Guest suites
- Kids’ playrooms
- Wine rooms and custom bars
- Work-from-home offices
- Multi-purpose living spaces
Basement Remodeling Throughout St. Louis
Aptitude Design & Build provides basement remodeling and finishing services throughout the St. Louis region, including Clayton, Ladue, Chesterfield, Frontenac, Kirkwood, Town & Country, West County and South City. We also serve homeowners in St. Charles and surrounding communities.
FAQs
How long does a basement remodel take?

Most basement remodeling projects in St. Louis take between 6–12 weeks once construction begins. Timelines vary depending on the complexity of the project, permit approvals, and custom features included.

Does finishing a basement increase home value?

Yes. A finished basement can increase usable square footage and improve resale appeal, especially when the space includes functional living areas, bathrooms, or entertainment features.

Can you add a bathroom to a basement?

Yes. Many basement remodeling projects include adding a bathroom, wet bar, or kitchenette. Our team handles the plumbing, electrical, permitting, and construction required for these additions.

Do you handle permits for basement remodeling projects?

Yes. Aptitude Design & Build manages permitting and inspections for basement remodeling projects throughout St. Louis, St. Charles, and surrounding communities.

Why hire a design-build contractor for a basement remodel?

A design-build approach brings the design and construction of your basement renovation under one team. Aptitude manages space planning, material selections, budgeting, permitting and construction, helping create a more coordinated process from the initial concept through project completion.

How Much Does a Basement Remodel Cost in St. Louis?

Basement remodeling costs vary depending on the size of the space, the level of finish, and the features included. Elements such as bathrooms, custom bars, guest suites, home offices, fitness rooms, and entertainment areas can all influence the overall investment. Most homeowners invest between $50,000 and $200,000+ depending on the scope of the project and the complexity of the design.

How long does a bathroom remodel take?

Most bathroom remodeling projects in St. Louis take between 4–8 weeks once construction begins. Larger renovations involving layout changes, custom tile work, or plumbing modifications may take longer.

Does bathroom remodeling increase home value?

Yes. Updated bathrooms are one of the most valuable home improvements for both resale appeal and everyday comfort. Many homeowners remodel bathrooms to improve functionality, modernize finishes, and increase overall home value.

Do you offer design-build bathroom remodeling?

Yes. Aptitude Design & Build is a full-service design-build remodeling firm serving St. Louis and St. Charles. Our team manages both the design and construction phases of your project, creating a more streamlined and collaborative remodeling experience.

Can you reconfigure the layout of a bathroom?

Yes. Many bathroom remodeling projects involve improving the layout to create better flow, larger showers, additional storage, or more usable space. Our team evaluates the existing layout and develops a plan tailored to your goals and the structure of the home.

Can I stay in my home during a bathroom remodel?

In most cases, yes. Many homeowners remain in their homes during bathroom remodeling projects, although access to the bathroom being renovated will be limited during construction.

Do you handle permits in St. Louis?

Yes. Aptitude Design & Build handles permitting and inspections for bathroom remodeling projects throughout St. Louis, St. Charles, and surrounding communities.

Factors such as custom tile work, walk-in showers, freestanding tubs, custom vanities, accessibility features, and plumbing or layout changes can all impact the overall investment. General Home Remodeling in St. Louis

Aptitude Design & Build provides custom home remodeling services for homeowners throughout St. Louis and St. Charles. From single-room renovations to large-scale home transformations, our design-build team helps homeowners reimagine their spaces with thoughtful design, quality craftsmanship, and a streamlined remodeling experience.

Whether you’re updating an older home, improving functionality for a growing family, modernizing outdated spaces, or creating a more cohesive layout throughout the home, we guide homeowners through every stage of the remodeling process — from planning and design through construction and final completion.

Why Homeowners Remodel Their Homes

Many homeowners throughout St. Louis choose to remodel instead of move, allowing them to improve the functionality, comfort, and value of their current home while remaining in the neighborhoods they love.

Home remodeling projects may help homeowners:

- Improve flow and functionality
- Modernize outdated layouts and finishes
- Create open-concept living spaces
- Increase usable square footage
- Improve storage and organization
- Adapt homes for changing lifestyles
- Increase long-term home value
- Personalize the home to better reflect their style and needs
How Much Does Home Remodeling Cost in St. Louis?

Home remodeling costs vary significantly depending on the size of the project, structural changes involved, material selections, and the age of the home. In the St. Louis area, remodeling projects may range from smaller targeted renovations to large-scale whole-home transformations exceeding several hundred thousand dollars.

Projects involving custom finishes, layout modifications, additions, or extensive structural work may require a larger investment.

Our Home Remodeling Process
Design Consultation

We begin by understanding your goals, priorities, and how you want your home to function both now and in the future.

Concept and Space Planning

Our design-build team develops a customized plan that improves layout, functionality, flow, and overall livability.

Material Selections and Budgeting

We guide homeowners through finish selections, fixtures, cabinetry, flooring, lighting, and budgeting to create a clear project plan.

Construction and Project Management

Our team manages all phases of construction, coordinating trades, scheduling, communication, and quality control throughout the project.

Final Walkthrough and Completion

We complete a final walkthrough to ensure every detail meets expectations before project completion.

Homeowners may also want to explore our kitchen remodeling, bathroom remodeling, and basement remodeling services.

FAQs
What is the difference between remodeling and renovating?

Remodeling typically involves changing the layout, structure, or functionality of a space, while renovating generally refers to updating finishes or restoring an existing space without major structural changes.

Do you offer design-build remodeling services?

Yes. Aptitude Design & Build is a full-service design-build remodeling firm serving St. Louis and St. Charles. Our team manages both the design and construction phases of the project, creating a more streamlined and collaborative experience.

Can you remodel older homes in St. Louis?

Yes. Many homes throughout St. Louis feature older layouts, aging infrastructure, or outdated finishes. Our team has experience remodeling older homes while improving functionality, preserving character where desired, and updating systems to meet modern needs.

How long does a home remodeling project take?

Project timelines vary depending on the size and complexity of the renovation. Smaller remodeling projects may take several weeks, while larger whole-home remodels can take several months.

Can I live in my home during remodeling?

In many cases, yes. Some homeowners remain in their homes during remodeling projects, although larger renovations may require temporary adjustments to daily routines depending on the scope of work.

Do you handle permits in St. Louis?

Yes. Aptitude Design & Build handles permitting and inspections for remodeling projects throughout St. Louis, St. Charles, and surrounding communities.

ST. CHARLES KITCHEN REMODEL OPEN CONCEPT
Open-Concept Kitchen Remodel Designed for Gathering

This kitchen remodel completely transformed the way the homeowners use their main level. By removing a major structural wall, reworking the kitchen layout and creating an oversized island at the center of the space, Aptitude Design & Build turned what had been a more closed-off kitchen and family room into one bright, connected gathering space.

Creating a More Open and Functional Main Level

The homeowners wanted more than an updated kitchen. They wanted to change the way the kitchen related to the rest of their home.

The original kitchen felt separated from the family room, limiting both the flow and functionality of the main level. The goal was to create a kitchen that worked better for everyday cooking while providing plenty of room for family and entertaining.

Opening the kitchen to the family room would also allow natural light to travel more freely through the space and make the two rooms feel like one cohesive living area.

Removing the Load-Bearing Wall

The most significant part of the remodel was removing the wall between the kitchen and family room.

This wasn't simply a matter of demolition. The wall was load-bearing and supported the entire second floor of the home.

Before it could be removed, the structure above had to be temporarily supported. Aptitude then installed the appropriate beam and support system to safely transfer the loads previously carried by the wall.

Once the structural work was complete, the impact was dramatic.

Instead of two separate rooms, the homeowners now have one large, open space where the kitchen and family room naturally flow together.

An Oversized Island at the Center of the Kitchen

With the wall gone, the new layout created room for one of the kitchen's defining features: a large central island.

The oversized island provides substantial prep space, storage and seating, making it both a hardworking part of the kitchen and a natural gathering place.

A second sink was incorporated into the island to create another prep area. This is particularly useful when more than one person is cooking or entertaining, allowing different tasks to happen simultaneously without everyone competing for the same workspace.

The overall layout also creates better work zones between the main sink, cooktop, refrigerator and other appliances.

A Bright, Warm and Timeless Design

The homeowners wanted the new kitchen to feel bright and clean without feeling cold.

Light shaker-style cabinetry around the perimeter helps keep the room open and airy, while the island cabinetry features a contrasting stained wood finish. The warmer wood gives the island a furniture-like quality and creates a natural focal point in the room.

Light countertops with prominent veining introduce movement and character while complementing the understated cabinetry.

Wood flooring brings additional warmth to the kitchen and creates visual continuity with the adjoining living spaces—an especially important consideration now that the rooms are open to one another.

A Backsplash That Goes Beyond the Expected

One of the details that gives this kitchen its custom feel is the backsplash.

Rather than stopping the tile at the most obvious points, the vertically installed backsplash continues around the kitchen and extends above and around the windows.

It's a relatively simple design decision that has a significant visual impact. The additional tile makes the entire installation feel deliberate and complete while adding subtle texture to the light, neutral palette.

Lighting Designed to Keep the Space Open

The lighting was kept clean and unobtrusive to complement the open design.

Recessed ceiling lighting provides overall illumination without adding visual clutter, while under-cabinet lighting provides useful task lighting across the countertops.

Natural light also plays a much bigger role in the remodeled space. With the wall between the kitchen and family room removed, light can move throughout the main level rather than being contained within individual rooms.

Appliances Integrated Into the New Layout

Stainless steel appliances complement the cabinetry and finishes while giving the kitchen a polished, professional feel.

The new kitchen includes a large refrigerator, built-in oven, gas cooktop and hood. Their locations were considered as part of the overall kitchen plan so the appliances work with the different prep, cooking and cleanup zones rather than interrupting them.

Additional Storage and Serving Space

The remodel extends beyond the primary kitchen cabinetry.

Built-in cabinetry and open shelving were incorporated into the adjoining area, providing additional storage and a convenient place for serving and display.

The materials and design connect visually with the kitchen, allowing this area to feel like a natural extension of the room rather than a separate feature.

Coordinating a Complex Kitchen Remodel

Removing the load-bearing wall was the project's biggest technical challenge, but a remodel of this scale involves much more than structural work.

Cabinetry, countertops, plumbing, electrical, appliances, tile, flooring and finish carpentry all have to come together in the correct sequence.

Aptitude coordinated those different elements throughout the project, with each decision considered as part of the larger design.

The result is a kitchen that feels intentional from one end of the space to the other.

More Than a Kitchen Transformation

Perhaps the biggest success of this project is that the transformation doesn't stop at the kitchen.

Removing the wall changed the way the entire main level functions. The kitchen and family room now feel like one large, connected space with more natural light, better flow and significantly more room for people to gather.

The oversized island may be the centerpiece, but it's the combination of the new layout, warm wood tones, light cabinetry, detailed backsplash and connection to the family room that makes the finished space work.

This wasn't simply an update to an existing kitchen.

It changed the way the homeowners can use and enjoy their home.

BALLWIN BATHROOM REMODEL

For the Galloway homeowners, the goal was to transform an outdated, awkward primary bathroom into a contemporary, spa-like retreat designed around how they actually use the space each day.

The existing bathroom had an old-fashioned corner tub, a small shower, a toilet that was completely open to the rest of the room, and a layout that made the bathroom feel more confined than it needed to be. Because both homeowners often get ready at the same time, creating more personal space and improving the overall flow were just as important as updating the look.

Rethinking the Layout

The biggest transformation came from reconsidering the relationship between the bathroom and adjoining closet.

We removed a wall and shifted part of the bathroom into the existing closet footprint, allowing us to widen the room and create a much more functional layout. A new bathroom entrance was created, and instead of sharing one vanity area, the homeowners now have two separate vanities, giving each person their own space for getting ready.

We also created a dedicated toilet area for greater privacy. Rather than taking the new partition wall all the way to the ceiling, we intentionally stopped it short, allowing natural light to continue flowing throughout the bathroom.

The new layout also made room for a significantly larger shower designed for two, along with a deep soaking tub positioned to take advantage of the peaceful wooded view behind the home.

Natural Stone + Mixed Metals

One of the standout features of the finished bathroom is the Italian quartzite used throughout the floor and shower. The stone is quarried in relatively small quantities in Italy and has a beautiful natural character that becomes especially apparent as the light moves across it.

Rather than matching every fixture and finish, we intentionally mixed metals throughout the bathroom, including brushed gold and chrome. When used thoughtfully, mixed metals add dimension and keep a contemporary bathroom from feeling overly coordinated.

A statement chandelier brings another layer of sophistication to the room, while backlit mirrors provide both a modern design feature and highly functional, face-forward lighting for getting ready.

A Spa-Like Bathroom Designed for Two

The finished bathroom isn't simply larger—it works considerably better for the homeowners' everyday routine.

They can get ready simultaneously without feeling like they're on top of one another. Each person has a dedicated vanity. The oversized shower comfortably accommodates two people. And the deep soaking tub creates a quiet place to relax while looking out toward the woods.

The result is a peaceful, contemporary primary bathroom that feels almost like a private spa while still being highly practical for everyday life.

One of the challenges of creating such a large, open shower didn't become apparent until construction was well underway: how do you actually get an enormous piece of shower glass into the finished space? It was an important logistical consideration that required careful planning and coordination, but the expansive glass ultimately helps preserve the bathroom's open feeling and showcases the stonework rather than visually dividing the room.

What Makes the Galloway Bathroom Special

What makes this project stand out is how completely the design grew from the homeowners' needs. Rather than simply replacing an outdated bathroom with newer finishes, we reconsidered the entrance, borrowed space from the closet, separated the vanities, created privacy around the toilet and dramatically expanded the shower.

Every decision helped create the experience the homeowners originally asked for: a clean, contemporary, spa-like bathroom with enough room for two people to comfortably begin and end their day.
